task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I found your account, John. Before we dig in, I want to make sure I'm troubleshooting the right line.

You have three lines on your account:
- **555-123-2001** — line L1001, Active
- **555-123-2002** — line L1002, Active (Premium Plan) — this is the number you gave me
- **555-123-2003** — line L1003, currently Suspended (since 2025-02-01)

Which line is having the mobile data problem? Also — are you currently outside your home network area (traveling), or at home?
turns.execution_output: User: It's the 555-123-2002 line — that's my main one. And yes, I'm actually traveling right now; I'm in France at the moment.

turns.thought:
Good to know. I've checked line **555-123-2002** (L1002), and I found two relevant things:

1. **International roaming is already enabled** on your line — so that part is fine for France.
2. **You've used up your plan's data allowance.** You've used **15.1 GB out of your 15.0 GB limit** for this billing cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28). That is almost certainly why data has either stopped or become very slow.

To get you back up and running today, you can **refuel data** on this line. Your Premium Plan rate is **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum I can add is **2 GB**.

How much data would you like to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?
turns.execution_output: User: Since I'm abroad and relying on data entirely — no Wi-Fi available here — I'll go with the full 2 GB, please. That should hopefully get me through until the cycle resets.

turns.thought: Adding 2 GB now at $2.00/GB — that's **$4.00**, which will be added to your bill.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Done! I've added **2 GB of data** to line **555-123-2002** for **$4.00**, which has been charged to your account. The refuel is confirmed on the line.

Since you're abroad, here are a few things to check on your phone to make sure the data actually flows:

- **Data Roaming is ON** on the device. I've confirmed roaming is enabled on your line from our side, but the phone itself also has a Data Roaming switch that needs to be on.
- **Airplane Mode is OFF.**
- **Mobile Data is ON.**

Could you check those settings and let me know if data is working now? If it's still slow or not connecting, tell me and we'll keep troubleshooting.

A couple of extra notes while you're here:

- Your new allowance lasts until your **cycle resets on 2025-02-28**.
- I also noticed **line 555-123-2003 has been suspended since 2025-02-01**. If you'd like me to look into reinstating that one too, just let me know.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check those settings on my phone now.

turns.thought:
Yes — turn both of those on. Here's the full rundown of what I'd suggest, in order:

**1. Turn Mobile Data ON**
Yes, go ahead and switch this on. This is the main switch for using cellular data, and it's currently off, which alone would stop your data entirely.

**2. Turn Data Roaming ON**
Yes, switch this on too. Roaming is already enabled on your line from our side (I verified that), so the phone-side switch is the missing piece for using data in France.

**3. Your phone is on 2G — change this**
This is likely the main reason your data is *slow* when it does work. 2G isn't fast enough for normal browsing or apps. Go into your network/mobile network settings and change your **preferred network mode to 4G/5G (or "4G/5G preferred")** rather than 2G. That should give you a much better speed.

**4. The VPN**
Your signal is showing as **Poor**, which is a separate concern. A VPN can sometimes add overhead and slow things down further. I'd suggest **disconnecting the VPN temporarily** and testing your data again — that way we can rule it out as a contributing factor. You can reconnect it afterwards if it makes no difference.

Go ahead and make those changes, then let me know:
- What your **signal and network type** show now (e.g. 4G/5G, and how many bars)
- Whether **data is working and how fast** it feels

One thing to flag: if your **signal is still Poor** after switching off 2G, that's a coverage/connection issue rather than a settings one, and we'd want to look at that next — possibly a SIM check. Let me know how you get on.

Great progress — that's a big improvement. You went from **Poor/2G to Excellent/5G**, and mobile data plus roaming are now on with the VPN disconnected. That's the bulk of the configuration issues resolved.

On your two questions:

**1. Data Saver — yes, turn it OFF**

That icon is worth acting on. Data Saver restricts background data and can reduce your effective throughput, so it could well be holding you below "Excellent." Go ahead and switch **Data Saver OFF**, then run the speed test again and let me know the result.

**2. On "Good" vs. "Excellent" — I want to be straight with you**

I don't want to overpromise here. Your 55 Mbps result is labelled "Good," which is below "Excellent," but I can't guarantee that turning off Data Saver alone will push it to the top tier — actual throughput depends on local network conditions in your area in France, how busy the local mast is, and the roaming partner network you're connected to. Those aren't things I can change from my side.

What I *can* say is that Data Saver is the one remaining device-side setting that could be limiting you, so let's eliminate it first.

**Please do this:**
1. Turn **Data Saver OFF**
2. Re-run the **speed test**
3. Tell me the result

If it comes back **Excellent** — we're done, and you're all set for the rest of your trip.

If it's **still "Good" or lower**, then we've exhausted the settings and account-side fixes available to me, and it's likely a network-capacity or roaming-partner issue rather than anything on your phone or your plan. In that case I'll transfer you to a human agent in technical support who can investigate the network side further.

One other thing on your account, unrelated to speed: your line **555-123-2003 is still suspended** (since 2025-02-01). Just say the word if you'd like me to look into that as well.

That's fantastic news — 275 Mbps and "Excellent"! Great result, and thanks for your patience working through the steps with me.

Here's a quick summary of what we did on line **555-123-2002**, in case you need it for reference:

- **Refuelled 2 GB of data** (charged $4.00 at your Premium Plan rate of $2.00/GB), because you'd used 15.1 GB of your 15.0 GB limit
- **Turned Mobile Data ON**
- **Turned Data Roaming ON** (roaming was already enabled on your line from our side)
- **Switched network mode off 2G to 4G/5G** — took you from Poor/2G to Excellent/5G
- **Disconnected the VPN**
- **Turned Data Saver OFF** — the final fix that got you to 275 Mbps

Two things worth keeping in mind:

- Your data allowance (15 GB + 2 GB refuel) **resets on 2025-02-28**. You're nearly through the refuel already, so if you run into trouble again before the reset, just get in touch and we can look at adding more data.
- The **$4.00 refuel charge** will appear on an upcoming bill.

No problem at all on line 555-123-2003 — I'll leave that one alone.

Enjoy the rest of your trip in France, and have a great day!
